iOS 27.2 is coming out sooner than you might expect. iOS 27.1 will focus solely on changes for the iPhone Duo, so new features for other users will have to wait until iOS 27.2. Here's when the update is expected to launch.

iOS 27.2 is confirmed to launch in October, likely the end of the month

Apple is currently testing iOS 27.2, and has been for weeks. Testing started much earlier than a typical x.2 release, and there's a reason for it.

The iPhone Duo launches October 23, with iOS 27.1 preinstalled. All signs point to no other iPhones getting that update, skipping straight to 27.2.

Apple has limited iOS 27.1 to the iPhone Duo exclusively, which keeps it from being exposed during testing, keeping more of the software experience under wraps. That's why iOS 27.2 is what's being tested right now.

When is iOS 27.2 launching? We know it's October.

When iOS 27 debuted last month, Apple said that Siri AI would get support for French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish "next month".

Those new Siri languages are included in iOS 27.2, confirming the October release timeline. Other new features coming with iOS 27.2 include:

  • User profiles in the Apple TV app
  • Dual camera simultaneous shooting in Group FaceTime
  • New Suggestions feature in Messages
  • Major revamp of the "Up Next" feature in Apple Podcasts
  • Apple Books design update

Routinely, Apple releases the first feature update after a major new system version at the end of October, and that isn't expected to change this year. The most likely launch window is the week of October 26.

iOS 27.2 could come slightly earlier than expected, especially if new hardware launching next week comes preinstalled with it. However, rumored Home products may not ship immediately. Instead, the first orders may arrive the last week of October, right alongside the iOS 27.2, tvOS 27.2, and HomePod 27.2 launches.

Which upcoming iPhone features are you most looking forward to? Let us know in the comments.
